$comment: Single source of truth for the cross-app audit. 03-sharing-matrix.md, 12-coupling.md and the acyclicity assertion are all rendered from this file by scripts/cross-app/. Edit here, then re-run render-matrix.mjs and check-acyclic.mjs. Fields: id, producer domain, consumer domain, what flows, class (IS|CAN|MUST), necessity (Essential|High value|Nice to have), why (taxonomy numbers 1-8), shape (1-6 from 07-plumbing.md), status (proposed|rejected), gap bucket, and for rejected items the rule it failed.

shapes.2: Backend aggregate endpoint owned by the consumer

connections.flows: employment status change (terminated, contract ended) revokes app access
connections.shortFlows: revoke app access on employment end

connections.flows: supplier identity and name for accounts-payable bills
billable logged hours per project, so hours can be invoiced and unbilled time surfaced
employee pay rate, aggregated server-side into a project labour cost
approved leave dates, to warn before assigning work due during them
signed contract (plan, mrr, seats, customer) to draft an invoice
customer identity for invoices, replacing four free-text client fields
outstanding and overdue balance on the customer page, and before extending credit
connections.shortFlows: outstanding balance on the customer page

connections.flows: open ticket count and last ticket date on the customer page
connections.shortFlows: ticket history on the customer page

connections.flows: one stock quantity and one cost price per sellable item, instead of two independent numbers
connections.shortFlows: one stock number and one cost per item

connections.flows: current assigned workload on the employee page, before assigning more
connections.reason: Nice to have, not Essential or High value. A manager who wants this can open Flow, which is one click away and shows more than a summary widget would.

connections.flows: budget consumed against a project
connections.reason: Finance holds no project_id on any expense, invoice or bill, so there is no project budget to consume. This needs a new concept (project cost allocation) before it is a connection, and that concept belongs to Finance, not to this audit.

connections.flows: bill and payment history on the supplier page
connections.shortFlows: bill history on the supplier page

connections.flows: inventory valuation total for the balance sheet
connections.shortFlows: inventory valuation for the balance sheet

connections.flows: hired candidate becomes an employee record without retyping the person
one resolver so a person or company means one thing product-wide
connections.shortFlows: one resolver for people and companies

connections.flows: collapse hr_staff and hr_employees into one person record with one pay rate
connections.shortFlows: one person record, one pay rate

connections.flows: day-close takings posted to the journal
connections.reason: POS has no operator surface in this repo and serves a separate terminal application, so the consuming screen cannot be built or tested here. Real, valuable, and out of scope for a frontend monorepo audit: it belongs to the POS repo's own roadmap.

connections.flows: zero stock or passed expiry blocks a sale
connections.reason: Same reason as POS->FIN-01: the consumer is the POS terminal repo. Subsumed by ERP->POS-01, which fixes the underlying duplicate stock number that makes this gate impossible to enforce correctly in the first place.

connections.flows: labour cost per period for the cost side of every margin metric
appointment history as customer activity
connections.reason: Booking has no app in this repo and booking.Appointment carries no customer id, only a staff id. Nobody would notice this shipping because nobody can create an appointment through a RTYLR surface today.

connections.flows: project hours and delivery metrics in the analytics app
connections.reason: Already partly built: insights declares RoadmapProject.project_id and WorkloadEntry.user_id and Flow has its own flow_insights module. Adding a second path to the same numbers would duplicate an existing aggregate rather than connect anything new.

connections.flows: tenant, user, team, app entitlement and config
connections.reason: Already the product's one working cross-domain contract. Documented as the precedent every other connection should imitate, not as new work.

connections.flows: purchase order received-but-unbilled and outstanding commitments, for the payables picture
bill approved and paid, so a purchase order stops looking outstanding
connections.shortFlows: bill settlement closes the purchase order

connections.flows: reorder suggestions already exist; surface them where purchasing happens
connections.reason: Intra-domain, and already built: apps/erp/src/features/reorder/useReorderSuggestions.ts calls listReorderSuggestions today. Not a crossing.

connections.flows: cost to serve a customer, from support time logged against them
connections.reason: Requires time to be logged against a customer, which no contract supports: hr.TimeEntryPayload carries project_id and task_id only (packages/voxie/api/hr/time_entry/v1/models.onk:12). Needs a new concept (customer-attributable time) that nobody has asked for.

connections.flows: ticket volume and resolution time as an operations metric
connections.reason: Support has no operator app in this repo, so no tenant is generating ticket data through a RTYLR surface. Reporting on an empty table is not a feature a customer notices.

connections.flows: staff availability and shift coverage behind a bookable slot
connections.reason: No booking app exists in apps/, so the consuming surface cannot be built or degraded-tested here. Worth revisiting the day a booking app is scaffolded; the contracts and backend modules are already in place.

connections.flows: cycle commitments vs scheduled shifts, to catch overtime committed twice
connections.reason: hr.shift keys attendance on staff_id while flow work days key on employee_id, and the bridge between those id spaces is a nullable column (02-entity-graph.md). Blocked behind HR->HR-01; re-evaluate after the person record is unified.

connections.flows: revenue actuals as the numerator for every margin metric
connections.reason: Already flowing, and in the wrong direction: apps/finance reads /insights/financial/cash-flow rather than Insights reading Finance. Logged as an inversion in 10-doc-drift.md; fixing the direction is a refactor of existing code, not a new connection.

connections.flows: order history and lifetime spend on the customer page
connections.shortFlows: order history on the customer page

connections.flows: sales by item and by hour for the analytics app
connections.reason: Already built: dash reads 9 pos endpoints and insights declares BestSeller/SlowMover over erp products. A third path to the same numbers adds an edge without adding an answer.

connections.flows: product cost, to turn revenue-by-product into margin-by-product
team member invited in dash becomes an employee record
connections.reason: Negative ROI: inviting a login and hiring a person are genuinely different acts, and auto-creating an employee for every invited contractor or agency user would create records an HR admin then has to clean up. The reverse edge (REC->HR-01) is the one worth building.

connections.flows: unpaid subscription suspends app access
connections.reason: Confuses two different money flows. hub.billing already handles what the tenant owes RTYLR (packages/voxie/api/hub/billing/v1); finance.invoices is what the tenant's own customers owe the tenant. Connecting them would suspend a customer's account because their client paid late.

connections.flows: customer counts, churn and segment size
connections.reason: insights already ships a customers area and crm ships its own dashboard capability (packages/voxie/api/crm/dashboard/v1). Duplicating the rollup would give two numbers for one question, which is worse than one.

connections.flows: payroll run total posted to the journal as a labour expense
product catalogue inside campaign composition
connections.reason: Technically trivial and nobody would notice. Campaign copy is written as free text today and a product picker saves one paste. The most tempting kind of low-value edge: cheap, obvious, and permanently owned by someone.

connections.flows: terminated employee loses terminal access
connections.reason: Correct and important, but the consumer is the POS terminal repo. Folded into HR->HUB-01, which revokes at the entitlement layer every surface reads, rather than adding a per-surface revocation edge.

emptyCellReasons.infra: common holds auth and pagination wrappers, not business data. Every app already depends on it as infrastructure; there is no business fact to share in either direction.
emptyCellReasons.console: console is RTYLR's own cross-tenant admin surface. A tenant domain reading it would cross a tenancy boundary, and console reading a tenant domain is already its whole job. Deliberately not connected.
emptyCellReasons.no-consumer-surface: The consuming domain has no operator surface in this repo (booking and support have contracts and backend modules but no app; pos serves the separate terminal repo). A connection whose consumer cannot be built here fails bar rule 3.
emptyCellReasons.no-producer-data: The producing domain holds no fact this consumer needs. Verified against the producer's entity list in 02-entity-graph.md.
emptyCellReasons.insights-is-terminal: insights is a read-only projection layer. It consumes; nothing should consume it, because a second domain reading insights would depend on a derived number instead of its source. Finance already violates this once (see 10-doc-drift.md).
emptyCellReasons.would-invert: The natural direction of this pair is the reverse edge, which is listed. Adding this direction too would create a cycle and breaks rule 2.
emptyCellReasons.hub-already-shared: hub is the tenant, user, team and entitlement domain that every app already reads; that crossing is built and working (HUB->ALL-01). Its outbound cells are marked here rather than re-proposed.
